text:
J.T. Miller is the Rangers' captain, back in New York after the Vancouver years, and his first trip back to Rogers Arena on Friday came with all the old storylines, including the Province asking whether anyone still cares about him and Elias Pettersson. The Rangers won 5-1, and Miller had two assists.

His season is a good example of results lagging play. He has 16 points in 21 games but only four goals on 7.4 expected, and none in his last seven games on 3.3 expected. Worse luck than that: the Rangers have scored 10.4 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. With him out there at five on five, they take 62% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), almost 14 points better than without him. That's elite play-driving, and it's the reason the New York Post's complaints about his production should fade.

Evolving-Hockey had a similar story last season: around replacement level by results, but 86th-percentile play-driving and far better by chance quality. Our talent range has him near 62 points. If the shots start going in, the Rangers' best stretch of the season gets better.
